s.en: search for files in a directory hierarchy
s.es: busca archivos y directorios recorriendo un árbol según condiciones

p.es: Dónde empezar a buscar (uno o varios directorios). Sin ruta busca en el actual.
p.en: Where to start searching (one or more directories). With none, searches the current one.

tip: Las condiciones se evalúan de izquierda a derecha: pon «-delete» o «-exec» al final, nunca antes de las pruebas.

o.es: Nombre que coincide con el patrón (distingue mayúsculas; usa comillas para que la shell no expanda el *).
o.en: Name matching the pattern (case-sensitive; quote it so the shell does not expand the *).

o.es: Como -name pero sin distinguir mayúsculas.
o.en: Like -name but case-insensitive.

o.es: La ruta completa coincide con el patrón.
o.en: The whole path matches the pattern.

o.es: La ruta completa coincide con la expresión regular.
o.en: The whole path matches the regular expression.

o.es: Tipo: f archivo, d directorio, l enlace simbólico, b/c dispositivo, p tubería, s socket.
o.en: Type: f file, d directory, l symlink, b/c device, p pipe, s socket.

o.es: Tamaño: +100M (mayor de 100 MB), -10k (menor de 10 KB), 0 (vacío).
o.en: Size: +100M (larger than 100 MB), -10k (smaller than 10 KB), 0 (empty).

o.es: Modificado hace n días: +7 (más de 7 días), -1 (menos de 1 día).
o.en: Modified n days ago: +7 (more than 7 days), -1 (less than 1 day).

o.es: Accedido hace n días.
o.en: Accessed n days ago.

o.es: Cambio de metadatos hace n días.
o.en: Metadata changed n days ago.

o.es: Modificado hace n minutos.
o.en: Modified n minutes ago.

o.es: Modificado después que el archivo indicado.
o.en: Modified more recently than the given file.

o.es: Pertenece al usuario.
o.en: Owned by the user.

o.es: Pertenece al grupo.
o.en: Belongs to the group.

o.es: Permisos: 644 exacto, -644 «al menos estos», /222 «alguno de estos». Ej. -4000 = setuid.
o.en: Permissions: 644 exact, -644 "at least these", /222 "any of these". E.g. -4000 = setuid.

o.es: Desciende como máximo N niveles.
o.en: Descend at most N levels.

o.es: No actúa en los primeros N niveles.
o.en: Do not act on the first N levels.

o.es: Archivo o directorio vacío.
o.en: File or directory is empty.

o.es: Archivo ejecutable por ti.
o.en: File is executable by you.

o.es: Archivo legible por ti.
o.en: File is readable by you.

o.es: Archivo escribible por ti.
o.en: File is writable by you.

o.es: Imprime la ruta (acción por defecto).
o.en: Print the path (default action).

o.es: Imprime la ruta terminada en byte nulo (para xargs -0, seguro con espacios).
o.en: Print the path terminated by a null byte (for xargs -0, safe with spaces).

o.es: ¡BORRA lo encontrado! Colócalo siempre al final de las condiciones.
o.en: DELETES what is found! Always place it last among the tests.

o.es: Ejecuta un comando sobre lo encontrado; {} es el archivo; termina con \; (uno a uno) o + (todos juntos).
o.en: Run a command on what is found; {} is the file; end with \; (one by one) or + (all together).

o.es: Como -exec pero ejecuta desde el directorio del archivo (más seguro).
o.en: Like -exec but runs from the file's directory (safer).

o.es: Como -exec pero pide confirmación antes de cada ejecución.
o.en: Like -exec but asks for confirmation each time.

o.es: No entra en el directorio que coincide (para excluir carpetas).
o.en: Do not descend into the matched directory (to exclude folders).

o.es: Niega la condición siguiente (igual que «!»).
o.en: Negate the next test (same as "!").

o.es: Y lógico (por defecto entre condiciones).
o.en: Logical AND (default between tests).

o.es: O lógico.
o.en: Logical OR.

o.es: Sigue los enlaces simbólicos.
o.en: Follow symbolic links.

o.es: No cruza a otros sistemas de archivos.
o.en: Do not cross to other file systems.

o.es: Lista cada resultado en formato largo tipo «ls -dils».
o.en: List each result in "ls -dils" format.

o.es: Archivos cuyo propietario ya no existe.
o.en: Files whose owner no longer exists.

o.es: Mismo inodo que el archivo dado (enlaces duros).
o.en: Same inode as the given file (hard links).

Never follow symbolic links. This is the default behaviour. When find examines or prints information about files, and the file is a symbolic link, the information used shall be taken from the properties of the symbolic link itself.

Do not follow symbolic links, except while processing the command line arguments. When find examines or prints information about files, the information used shall be taken from the properties of the symbolic link itself.

Print diagnostic information; this can be helpful to diagnose problems with why find is not doing what you want. The list of debug options should be comma separated. Compatibility of the debug options is not guaranteed between releases of findutils. For a complete list of valid debug options, see the output of find -D help.

The find program reorders tests to speed up execution while preserving the overall effect; that is, predicates with side effects are not reordered relative to each other. The optimisations performed at each optimisation level are as follows. 0 Equivalent to optimisation level 1.

Measure times (for -amin, -atime, -cmin, -ctime, -mmin, and -mtime) from the beginning of today rather than from 24 hours ago. This option only affects tests which appear later on the command line. symbolic links. The same consideration applies to -newerXY, -anewer and -cnewer.

Changes the regular expression syntax understood by -regex and -iregex tests which occur later on the command line. To see which regular expression types are known, use -regextype help. The Texinfo documentation (see SEE ALSO) explains the meaning of and differences between the various types of regular expression.

Turn warning messages on or off. These warnings apply only to the command line usage, not to any conditions that find might encounter when it searches directories. The default behaviour corresponds to -warn if standard input is a tty, and to -nowarn otherwise.
A synonym for -depth, for compatibility with FreeBSD, NetBSD, MacOS X and OpenBSD.
The -delete action also implies -depth.

Read the starting points from file instead of getting them on the command line. In contrast to the known limitations of passing starting points via arguments on the command line, namely the limitation of the amount of file names, and the inherent ambiguity of file names clashing with option names, using this option allows to…
Print a summary of the command-line usage of find and exit.

Normally, find will emit an error message when it fails to stat a file. If you give this option and a file is deleted between the time find reads the name of the file from the directory and the time it tries to stat the file, no error message will be issued.
An alternate name for -xdev, for compatibility with some other versions of find.
Turns off the effect of -ignore_readdir_race.

This option is needed when searching filesystems that do not follow the Unix directory-link convention, such as CD-ROM or MS-DOS filesystems or AFS volume mount points. Each directory on a normal Unix filesystem has at least 2 hard links: its name and its `.' entry.
Print the find version number and exit.
for less than n,

Time of the last access of the current file is more recent than that of the last data modification of the reference file. If reference is a symbolic link and the -H option or the -L option is in effect, then the time of the last data modification of the file it points to is always used.

Time of the last status change of the current file is more recent than that of the last data modification of the reference file. If reference is a symbolic link and the -H option or the -L option is in effect, then the time of the last data modification of the file it points to is always used.

File is on a filesystem of type type. The valid filesystem types vary among different versions of Unix; an incomplete list of filesystem types that are accepted on some version of Unix or another is: ufs, 4.2, 4.3, nfs, tmp, mfs, S51K, S52K. You can use -printf with the %F directive to see the types of your filesystems.
Like -lname, but the match is case insensitive. If the -L option or the -follow option is in effect, this test returns false unless the symbolic link is broken.
It is normally easier to use the -samefile test instead.
Like -path. but the match is case insensitive.
Like -regex, but the match is case insensitive.
See -ipath. This alternative is less portable than -ipath.
File has less than, more than or exactly n hard links.

File is a symbolic link whose contents match shell pattern pattern. The metacharacters do not treat `/' or `.' specially. If the -L option or the -follow option is in effect, this test returns false unless the symbolic link is broken.

Succeeds if timestamp X of the file being considered is newer than timestamp Y of the file reference. The letters X and Y can be any of the following letters: a The access time of the file reference B The birth time of the file reference c The inode status change time of reference m The modification time of the file reference t…
No group corresponds to file's numeric group ID.
Always true.
See -path. This alternative is less portable than -path.

The same as -type unless the file is a symbolic link. For symbolic links: if the -H or -P option was specified, true if the file is a link to a file of type c; if the -L option has been given, true if c is `l'. In other words, for symbolic links, -xtype checks the type of the file that -type does not check.
(SELinux only) Security context of the file matches glob pattern.

If the removal failed, an error message is issued and find's exit status will be nonzero (when it eventually exits). Warning: Don't forget that find evaluates the command line as an expression, so putting -delete first will make find try to delete everything below the starting points you specified.

True; like -ls but write to file like -fprint. The output file is always created, even if the predicate is never matched. See the UNUSUAL FILENAMES section for information about how unusual characters in filenames are handled.

True; print the full file name into file file. If file does not exist when find is run, it is created; if it does exist, it is truncated. The file names /dev/stdout and /dev/stderr are handled specially; they refer to the standard output and standard error output, respectively.

True; like -printf but write to file like -fprint. The output file is always created, even if the predicate is never matched. See the UNUSUAL FILENAMES section for information about how unusual characters in filenames are handled.

Like -execdir but ask the user first in the same way as for -ok. If the user does not agree, just return false. If the command is run, its standard input is redirected from /dev/null. This action may not be specified together with the -files0-from option.

True; print format on the standard output, interpreting `\' escapes and `%' directives. Field widths and precisions can be specified as with the printf(3) C function. Please note that many of the fields are printed as %s rather than %d, and this may mean that flags don't work as you might expect.

Exit immediately (with return value zero if no errors have occurred). This is different to -prune because -prune only applies to the contents of pruned directories, while -quit simply makes find stop immediately. No child processes will be left running. Any command lines which have been built by -exec ... + or -execdir ...
